b1-grandepresion-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Before the Crash
b1-grandepresion-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos have watched a documentary about the crash of 1929, and Carlos asks what had happened before the crisis.
b1-grandepresion-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what had happened before the crisis.
cues: Say that many countries had already asked for large loans when the crisis came
Say that the prices of shares had risen a lot
b1-grandepresion-01.target: Cuando llegó la crisis, muchos países ya habían pedido grandes préstamos. Los precios de las acciones habían subido mucho.
b1-grandepresion-01.english: When the crisis came, many countries had already asked for large loans. The prices of shares had risen a lot.
b1-grandepresion-01.canDo: I can say what had already happened before another moment in the past, with *había* + past participle.

b1-grandepresion-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Coffee in Brazil
b1-grandepresion-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading a book about Latin America in the 1930s, and Meg asks what Brazil did about coffee.
b1-grandepresion-02.prompt: Tell Meg what Brazil did with coffee and what happened to the price.
cues: Say that the government burned part of the coffee
Say that, however, the price stayed low
b1-grandepresion-02.target: El gobierno quemó una parte del café. Sin embargo, el precio siguió bajo.
b1-grandepresion-02.english: The government burned part of the coffee. However, the price stayed low.
b1-grandepresion-02.canDo: I can show a contrast, with *sin embargo* and *no obstante*.

b1-grandepresion-03.title: Communicative Challenge: How Bad Was the Crisis?
b1-grandepresion-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos have been to a museum exhibition about the 1930s, and Carlos asks how bad the crisis was in Latin America.
b1-grandepresion-03.prompt: Tell Carlos how bad the crisis was.
cues: Say that the crisis of 1929 was the worst economic crisis Latin America had known
Say that the mining areas were among the most affected
b1-grandepresion-03.target: La crisis de 1929 fue la peor crisis económica que América Latina había conocido. Las zonas mineras fueron de las más afectadas.
b1-grandepresion-03.english: The crisis of 1929 was the worst economic crisis that Latin America had known. The mining areas were among the most affected.
b1-grandepresion-03.canDo: I can say that something is the worst, the most or the least, with a superlative.

b1-grandepresion-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Protecting Factories
b1-grandepresion-04.scenario: You are Carlos. After a class about the 1930s, Meg asks you how governments protected the factories of their countries.
b1-grandepresion-04.prompt: Tell Meg how governments protected the factories.
cues: Say that governments protected the country's factories
Say how: by means of higher tariffs
b1-grandepresion-04.target: Mediante aranceles más altos, los gobiernos protegieron las fábricas del país.
b1-grandepresion-04.english: By means of higher tariffs, governments protected the country's factories.
b1-grandepresion-04.canDo: I can say by what means something is done, with *mediante* + a noun.

b1-grandepresion-05.title: Communicative Challenge: A Turning Point
b1-grandepresion-05.scenario: You are Meg. You are summing up a chapter about the crisis of 1929 for Carlos.
b1-grandepresion-05.prompt: Sum up for Carlos what the crisis changed.
cues: Say in summary that the crisis was a turning point
Give two sides: industry grew in the cities, the countryside lost importance
b1-grandepresion-05.target: En resumen, la crisis de 1929 fue un punto de cambio. Por un lado, la industria creció; por otro lado, el campo perdió importancia.
b1-grandepresion-05.english: In summary, the crisis of 1929 was a turning point. On the one hand, industry grew; on the other hand, the countryside lost importance.
b1-grandepresion-05.canDo: I can build and close an explanation, with *por un lado ... por otro lado* and *en resumen*.

b1-grandepresion-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: The Great Depression
b1-grandepresion-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. After a class on the Great Depression, Meg asks you what you remember about the crisis and the way governments answered it.
cues: Say that many countries had already asked for large loans when the crisis came
Say how governments protected their factories
b1-grandepresion-consolidation.target: Cuando llegó la crisis, muchos países ya habían pedido grandes préstamos. Mediante aranceles más altos, los gobiernos protegieron las fábricas.
b1-grandepresion-consolidation.english: When the crisis came, many countries had already asked for large loans. By means of higher tariffs, governments protected the factories.
b1-grandepresion-consolidation.canDo: I can tell what had already happened before the crash, using the pluperfect.
